Typical error: adding the two changes (+5%). Percentages applied one after another do not add.

figure.title: Shuttle bus round trip between two sites

practice.question: What was the shuttle bus’s average speed for the whole round trip?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Times: 80 ÷ 75 = 1.067 h and 80 ÷ 40 = 2.000 h.
Typical error: averaging the two speeds (57.5 km/h). More time is spent at the lower speed, so the true average is lower.

figure.title: Plastic collected for recycling by four municipal schemes this year, and expected annual growth

mocks.question: If the figure for Westfield grows at its expected annual rate, compounded, approximately how many tonnes will be collected three years from now?
steps: Compound growth: 5,520 × 1.2³ = 5,520 × 1.7280 ≈ 9,539 tonnes.
Traps among the options: simple growth, 5,520 × (1 + 3 × 0.2) = 8,832 t, ignores compounding; compounding for only two years gives 7,949 t; compounding for four years gives 11,446 t.

figure.title: Regional development fund allocations by sector (€ million)

mocks.question: What percentage of the West region’s total allocation went to Digital?
steps: The West region’s total allocation is €2,440 million, of which Digital received €270 million.
Typical errors: dividing by the Digital column total (the region’s share of that sector) or by the remainder instead of the total.

figure.title: Rail routes: distance and average train speed

mocks.question: If the train’s average speed on the Riverton–Eastbay route rose to 160 km/h, approximately how many minutes would each journey save?
steps: Time = distance ÷ speed. Now: 193 ÷ 120 × 60 = 96.5 minutes. New: 193 ÷ 160 × 60 = 72.4 minutes.
Saving = 96.5 − 72.4 = 24.1, i.e. about 24 minutes.
Typical error: assuming journey time falls by the same percentage as speed rises.

figure.title: Containers handled at five ports (thousand units)

mocks.question: Which of the following ports recorded the largest percentage increase in containers handled between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Percentage change = (Year 2 − Year 1) ÷ Year 1 × 100:
Largest: Kingsford. Trap: Stonebridge has the largest increase in absolute terms (+210 thousand), but from a larger base.

figure.title: Translation requests and average turnaround by language unit

mocks.question: What is the average turnaround time per request in the four units combined?
steps: Total requests = 114. Weighted average = 1,397 ÷ 114 ≈ 12.25 days.
Typical error: the simple average of the four averages (13.00 days) ignores the different group sizes.

figure.title: Grant applications received and approval rate

mocks.question: If the number of applications stayed the same, how many additional applications from Sweden would need to be approved for its approval rate to reach 40%?
steps: Approvals needed = 900 × 40% = 360.
Currently approved = 900 × 18% = 162. Additional approvals = 198.
Typical error: giving the total number of approvals needed instead of the additional ones.

figure.title: A supplier’s price in Swiss franc and the exchange rate

mocks.question: In euro terms, by approximately what percentage has the supplier’s price risen between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Convert each year to euros: Year 1 394.00 ÷ 1.01 = €390.10; Year 2 417.64 ÷ 0.94 = €444.30.
Typical errors: quoting the 6% rise in local currency, or the change in the exchange rate alone; both ignore the other effect.

figure.title: Breakdown of an agency’s annual budget (total €605 million)

mocks.question: If spending on IT systems grows by 5% and every other item is frozen, what will the gap be between IT systems and Buildings?
steps: IT systems now = 28% × €605 million = €169.4 million; after +5%: €177.87 million.
Buildings = 6% × €605 million = €36.3 million.
Difference = €141.57 million ≈ €141.6 million. Typical error: adding 5 percentage points to the share instead of raising the amount by 5%.

figure.title: Unemployment rate (% of labour force)

mocks.question: By how many percentage points did the unemployment rate in Hungary rise between Year 3 and Year 5?
steps: A change in percentage points is the simple difference between the two rates: 9.6 − 7.2 = +2.4 points, i.e. a rise of 2.4 percentage points.
Typical error: computing the relative (percentage) change instead.

figure.title: Research grants awarded by field and region (€ million)

mocks.question: What percentage of the North region’s total grant funding went to Digital?
steps: The North region’s total allocation is €1,740 million, of which Digital received €720 million.
Typical errors: dividing by the Digital column total (the region’s share of that sector) or by the remainder instead of the total.

figure.title: Unemployment rate (% of labour force)

mocks.question: By how many percentage points did the unemployment rate in Romania fall between Year 1 and Year 5?
steps: A change in percentage points is the simple difference between the two rates: 4.1 − 7.0 = −2.9 points, i.e. a fall of 2.9 percentage points.
Typical error: computing the relative (percentage) change instead.

figure.title: Interpreting assignments in one quarter, by booth language

mocks.question: What is the ratio of assignments in Italian to assignments in Swedish, in its simplest form?
steps: Italian : Swedish = 56 : 40. Both numbers divide by 8, giving 7:5.
Typical error: reversing the order of the ratio (5:7).

figure.title: Staff numbers and average monthly salary by unit

mocks.question: What is the average monthly salary across all staff in the four units combined?
steps: Total staff = 66. Weighted average = 501,600 ÷ 66 ≈ €7,600.
Typical error: the simple average of the four averages (€6,900) ignores the different group sizes.

figure.title: Programme spending by sector (€ million)

mocks.question: By how many percentage points did Health’s share of total spending rise between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Change = 24.62 − 19.74 = +4.88 points, i.e. a rise of about 4.9 percentage points.
Typical errors: giving the percentage change in the amount spent, or the relative change in the share, instead of the change in percentage points.

figure.title: Grant applications received and approval rate

mocks.question: If the number of applications stayed the same, how many additional applications from France would need to be approved for its approval rate to reach 45%?
steps: Approvals needed = 3,000 × 45% = 1,350.
Currently approved = 3,000 × 24% = 720. Additional approvals = 630.
Typical error: giving the total number of approvals needed instead of the additional ones.

figure.title: Index of average house prices (Year 1 = 100)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did average house prices in Greece rise between Year 3 and Year 5?
steps: With index numbers, the percentage change between two years is (later index − earlier index) ÷ earlier index × 100.
Typical errors: subtracting the indices (9.5 is a change in index points, not per cent) or measuring from the base year (index − 100).

mocks.question: How much did the “Drafting legislation” course cost in total over Q1 to Q2 inclusive?
steps: Participants Q1 to Q2 inclusive: 25 + 24 = 49.
Typical errors: including the wrong quarters, using the whole year, or reading the wrong row of either table.

figure.title: Cases closed per month by three teams

mocks.question: How many cases would Team East need to close in June for its average over January to June to be exactly 45 per month?
steps: For an average of 45 over 6 months, the total must be 45 × 6 = 270.
January–May total = 21 + 31 + 37 + 29 + 43 = 161.
June must therefore be 270 − 161 = 109.
Typical errors: answering with the target itself (45) or with the current average (about 32).

figure.title: Passengers at five regional airports (thousands)

mocks.question: Which of the following airports recorded the largest percentage increase in passenger numbers between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Percentage change = (Year 2 − Year 1) ÷ Year 1 × 100:
Largest: Westfield. Trap: Eastbay has the largest increase in absolute terms (+160 thousand), but from a larger base.

figure.title: Price changes over two years

mocks.question: Compared with the start of Year 1, by what percentage are conference fees lower at the end of Year 2?
steps: Successive changes multiply: (1 − 0.2) × (1 + 0.2) = 0.9600.
So the price is −4.0% compared with the start, i.e. about 4.0% lower.
Typical error: adding the two changes (+0%). Percentages applied one after another do not add.

figure.title: Shuttle bus round trip between two sites

mocks.question: What was the shuttle bus’s average speed for the whole round trip?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Times: 80 ÷ 50 = 1.600 h and 80 ÷ 90 = 0.889 h.
Typical error: averaging the two speeds (70.0 km/h). More time is spent at the lower speed, so the true average is lower.

figure.title: Spending this year by programme and change compared with last year

mocks.question: Before this year’s change, what was the budget for “Youth employment schemes”?
steps: This year = last year × 1.3, so last year = this year ÷ 1.3.
Typical error: reducing this year’s figure by 30% applies the percentage to the wrong base.

figure.title: Price of a standard office laptop in four markets (fictitious prices and rates)

mocks.question: In euros, approximately how much more does a standard office laptop cost in the most expensive of the four markets than in the cheapest?
steps: Convert every price to euros by DIVIDING the local price by the number of units per €1:
Most expensive (JPY) − cheapest (ISK) ≈ €488.42 − €408.86 = €79.56, i.e. about €80.
Typical errors: ranking the markets by local price (the currencies are not comparable) or comparing the wrong pair of markets.

figure.title: Monthly rent of a liaison office in Japanese yen

mocks.question: Once both years are converted into euros, approximately what is the percentage by which the rent has risen?
steps: Typical errors: quoting the 10% rise in local currency, or the change in the exchange rate alone; both ignore the other effect.

figure.title: Breakdown of an agency’s annual budget (total €590 million)

mocks.question: Next year the Staff budget is to rise by 10% while all other items stay unchanged. By how much will the Staff budget then exceed the Training budget?
steps: Staff now = 13% × €590 million = €76.7 million; after +10%: €84.37 million.
Training = 7% × €590 million = €41.3 million.
Difference = €43.07 million ≈ €43.1 million. Typical error: adding 10 percentage points to the share instead of raising the amount by 10%.

figure.title: Staff by gender in four units

mocks.question: If the total number of staff in Unit C increases by 40% and the proportion of the “Women” group stays the same, how many will be in the “Women” group?
steps: Unit C has 25 (Women) and 20 (Men), 45 in total.
Shortcut: if the proportion is unchanged, the “Women” group also grows by 40%: 25 × 1.4 = 35.
Typical errors: adding the whole increase to one group (43) or calculating the other group instead.

figure.title: Passengers at regional airports (thousands)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did passenger numbers at regional airports in Sweden increase between Year 1 and Year 3?
steps: Percentage change uses the earlier value as the base: (930 − 845) ÷ 845 × 100.
= 85 ÷ 845 × 100 ≈ 10.1%, i.e. an increase of about 10.1%.
Typical errors: dividing by the Year 3 value (wrong base), or adding the two year-on-year percentage changes (percentages do not add).

figure.title: Rail routes: distance and average train speed

mocks.question: If the train’s average speed on the Westfield–Eastbay route rose to 120 km/h, approximately how many minutes would each journey save?
steps: Time = distance ÷ speed. Now: 162 ÷ 90 × 60 = 108.0 minutes. New: 162 ÷ 120 × 60 = 81.0 minutes.
Saving = 108.0 − 81.0 = 27.0, i.e. about 27 minutes.
Typical error: assuming journey time falls by the same percentage as speed rises.

figure.title: Population and public spending on culture in five regions of one country

mocks.question: Which of the following regions had the highest spending on culture per inhabitant?
steps: Spending per inhabitant = spending ÷ population (€ million ÷ million inhabitants = € per inhabitant):
Island region ≈ €239; Northern region ≈ €171; Coastal region ≈ €178; Southern region ≈ €91.
The highest figure is for the Island region. Trap: the Northern region has the largest total spending, but not the highest spending per inhabitant.

steps: Traps among the options: simple growth, 5,480 × (1 + 3 × 0.15) = 7,946 kW, ignores compounding; compounding for only two years gives 7,247 kW; compounding for four years gives 9,585 kW.
